inputs.note: All passages extracted from the twelve frozen train notes only. The withheld target was not read by the proposer.

proposer.discipline: Proposals are GeneratedInterpretation, not evidence. Nothing here is self-approved; entries have downstream effect only after operator adjudication.

labels.label: confinement of congruence methods to non-residues

entries.claim: Distinct mechanisms (per-class identities, finite covering, divisor factorization, class assembly with density) share the restriction that their congruence-carried reach eliminates only quadratic non-residue classes; quadratic-residue survivor classes remain outside all of them.
entries.proposed_property: confined_to_quadratic_nonresidues (working name): the method's coverage is carried by congruence relations that, by quadratic reciprocity, cannot catch quadratic-residue classes.
entries.scope: Asserted for es-01, es-02, es-03, es-10 (failure-side) with es-08 as the note that names the property as an obstruction. NOT asserted for es-05 (fails on growth rate, see L5) or es-07 (fails by definitional finiteness; its QR mention is about what remains beyond the bound, not about its mechanism's carrier).

evidence.passage: They resolve every class except those where n behaves like a perfect square to small moduli.

the congruence relations that carry polynomial identities can only eliminate quadratic *non*-residues. By quadratic reciprocity, no finite covering built from these identities can catch the quadratic-residue classes (see es-08).
the factorization view gives no global lattice organization of the solution set ... existence unforced for QR primes (boundary_statement).

the note that explains why the identity/covering families (es-01, es-02) all stall on the same classes ... It preserves — indeed pinpoints — the invariant that the whole identity/covering program confines to non-residues.
the exceptional set is thin but non-empty and infinite, and it is exactly the quadratic-residue survivor family.

entries.preserves_distinctions: es-01/es-02/es-03/es-10 remain four distinct mechanisms (local identity vs global covering vs divisor construction vs density assembly). This entry asserts a shared restriction, not sameness.

counterevidence.note: partial_success that explicitly 'adds no positivity for QR primes' — a non-failure outcome still preserving the property; relevant to challenge step 3 (success that preserves the invariant).

partial_success that designs around the restriction ('none of the admitted congruences is a quadratic residue', preserves 'Mordell non-residue restriction'); conjectural coverage. Mandatory contrast for any candidate built from this property.

entries.claim: In es-02, 'class union' is a constituent operation of the 'congruence covering' method: the covering system is built by unioning identity-admitting classes. Co-occurrence on one note is not evidence of interchangeability.
entries.scope: es-02 only. No alias is proposed; a support merge would double-count one note.

evidence.passage: it seeks a finite family of congruences whose union is all of Z.
notes: 'Seeks a finite union of solvable classes covering Z.' — the union is the means; the covering is the objective.

entries.preserves_distinctions: The global covering objective vs the class-level union operation, which es-02 itself distinguishes.

entries.claim: es-02's covering and es-10's assembly both construct unions of identity-admitting congruence classes; they differ on the demand placed on the union (exhaustive cover of Z vs bounded-density leftover). Not proposed as an alias.
entries.proposed_property: class_union_construction (working name): builds a union of congruence classes each admitting a polynomial identity.
entries.scope: es-02 and es-10. The exhaustive/existential vs density/estimative distinction is load-bearing: es-02 fails outright where es-10 reaches a thin-but-infinite exceptional set.

evidence.passage: choose finitely many moduli and residue classes so that every integer n falls into at least one class that admits an identity.
it works class by class (local identities) but its payoff is a global density statement about how thin the unsolved set is.

entries.preserves_distinctions: Exhaustive covering (existential, all of Z) vs density-driven assembly (counts survivors). Merging these as an alias would erase the variable that separates their outcome boundaries.

counterevidence.note: uses the exact label 'congruence covering' under partial_success (form-indexed, respecting the non-residue restriction). Any candidate involving covering must face this occurrence.

entries.claim: es-01, es-02 and es-10 all depend on class-local polynomial identities as the carrier of solvability; the dependency appears as operator (es-01), preserved property (es-02) and assumption (es-10).
entries.proposed_property: identity_carried_solvability (working name): solvability inside a congruence class is supplied by a fixed polynomial identity keyed to that class.
entries.scope: es-01, es-02, es-10 (failure-side). es-12 shares the dependency in form-indexed shape (partial_success contrast).

evidence.passage: For many residue classes of n, a fixed polynomial identity in n writes down 4/n = 1/x + 1/y + 1/z directly.
estimates the number of n ≤ N for which the conjecture is not yet settled by known congruence identities.

entries.preserves_distinctions: How each method uses the identities (locally, unioned, counted) stays distinct; only the dependency is shared.

counterevidence.note: associates a general polynomial to each of two solution forms — the same dependency arranged by form rather than by producing congruence, under partial_success.

entries.claim: es-05 fails for a different structural reason than the congruence family: its boundary is intrinsic growth rate (polylog average too slow to force existence), not quadratic-residue confinement. This distinction is potential counterevidence against over-generalizing L1.
entries.scope: es-05 vs the L1 cohort. If a future candidate claims 'all failure-side methods are QR-confined', es-05 refutes the universal reading.

evidence.passage: the average grows only polylogarithmically. For some Diophantine problems a positive average forces a solution to exist, but that argument needs at least polynomial growth.
it reasons about the distribution of solution counts across a large ensemble of primes rather than about any single n.

entries.preserves_distinctions: Ensemble/probabilistic posture vs congruence-carried constructive posture; growth-rate boundary vs residue-class boundary.

entries.claim: es-03's positivity-filtering by local congruences and es-01's resolved 'modular decomposition' both manipulate residue classes, but the train evidence does not establish that they are the same operation, a specialization, or a shared dependency beyond L1/L4.
entries.scope: Left unresolved; recorded so the gap is visible rather than silently absorbed into an alias.

evidence.passage: enumerating divisors of a quantity depending on n and applying local congruence filters to keep the denominators positive integers.

entries.preserves_distinctions: Filtering candidates for positivity vs decomposing the problem by modulus.
